messages:
Maria: quick follow-up to the cross-gpu aliasing RFC — ran the consolidation perf suite and saw a ~12% p99 latency regression when we enable aggressive coalesce across NVLink peers. looks like contention on the compact worker and stalled submission queues.
Kevin: hmm. do we have traces? which stage stalls? :thinking_face:
Maria: traces point to the compact worker holding a cross-gpu mutex while performing mapping validation + refcount updates. that blocks small realtime kernels. stack: compact_worker -> validate_aliases() -> remote_refcount_write()
Sophia: that's the pattern I'd feared. cross-gpu aliasing introduces synchronous metadata ops. we probably need an async two-phase handshake so hot paths don't block.
Raj: agree. proposal: move metadata validation into a pre-check phase that runs before the realtime path. realtime path receives a fast token if pre-check passed. fallback: synchronous copy if token absent.
Kevin: sketch API? I like explicit tokens.
Maria: rough sketch:

```
// preflight: idempotent, can run async
alias_ticket_t preflight_alias(src_gpu, dst_gpu, pages, flags);

// fast path from realtime
bool try_apply_alias(alias_ticket_t ticket);

// cleanup/revoke
void revoke_alias(alias_ticket_t ticket);
```

The ticket contains a compact-epoch + validation digest. try_apply_alias just checks ticket validity and flips a pointer table — cheap.
Sophia: two things: 1) who owns the memory migration mutex? 2) how do we make tickets resilient to eviction and transient topologies (nvlink down)?
Raj: ownership: ticket carries owner_hint (node/shard). revoke_alias will queue an async reconciliation if topology changed. for NVLink failures we expire ticket and force copy fallback.
Kevin: telemetry: we need counters for preflight_miss, try_apply_hit, forced_copy, ticket_expire. And a histogram for try_apply latency.
Maria: agreed. also add an opt-in policy per-tenant: some noisy tenants should never do cross-gpu aliasing (security/latency SLA).
Sophia: edge case: what about page-level refcounts racing with eviction scanner? if preflight passes but page gets demoted before try_apply runs.
Raj: preflight must pin a light reservation (soft-pin) that prevents immediate demotion but is revocable. revoke_alias removes pin. if eviction needs capacity it can steal soft-pins after a grace window.
Kevin: stealing pins means we need an admission protocol for reclaim. maybe keep a small global reserve to avoid stealing commonly-held tickets.
Maria: tradeoffs: pin adds memory pressure; not pinning invites races; the ticket TTL becomes tuning knob. propose default TTL 250ms and a tenant opt to increase.
Sophia: testing matrix: unit tests for ticket validity, fuzz for topology flips, stress tests with heavy eviction and microbatch under production load.
Raj: implementation plan: 1) wire preflight endpoint + ticket serialization 2) implement try_apply fast-path in runtime 3) add background reconciler for revoke/steal 4) telemetry and tenant policy flags.
Maria: ops note: add a controlled rollout behind feature flag (crossgpu-alias-v1). start with internal tenants and canary a couple dedicated clusters.
Kevin: one more thought — make ticket encryption-bound to KMS key per-cluster so customers can't forge tickets across clusters.
Sophia: +1 on KMS. also document API surface in internal rfc follow-up: aliasing lifetime, error codes (EXPIRED, TOPOLOGY_CHANGED, EVICTED, BACKPRESSURE), and SLAs (best-effort, not durable pin).
Maria: action items: Kevin to add telemetry hooks, Raj to prototype preflight API, Sophia to draft follow-up rfc section and tests, I'll coordinate rollout plan + canary list.
Kevin: I'll push a telemetry PR by EOD tomorrow.
Raj: starting prototype today, will ping when I have a basic ticket struct.
Sophia: drafting doc now, will add test scenarios by tomorrow.
evict-bot: [info] scheduled eviction-run in 30m; tickets with TTL < 60s may be reclaimed.
Maria: noted — will keep small TTLs during initial canary. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
